components.explanation: Hand-written canvas_item shader dims the 2D instrument cluster toward amber while FreightVan.headlights_on is true; a code-made driver fades night_amount by delta and reverses mid-fade.
Spatial fog shader with seven grouped uniforms and three textures (colour, normal, data); one shader, two ShaderMaterials on overlays beside the windshield and the driver's window.
Two samplers read one three-band image with and without source_color; unshaded quads show the values under Compatibility and a Forward+ comparison.
Godot's StandardMaterial3D conversion, annotated by the author, compared line-by-line and rendered beside the hand-written fog shader with the same textures.
Headless suites: uniform-list contract, real input timing at 30/60/144 fps, material/import audit, and the normal-map curl check calibrated on a Poly Haven pair.
project.godot names the Compatibility renderer (line 125), the main scene and the headlights (L) and left_window (J) input actions the captures press.

code_result_pairs.observation: Captured cluster pixels at night_amount 0.0/0.5/1.0 equal the hand predictions (18/18); 2.0 set from code goes darker, so hint_range did not clamp.
Pressing L fades the dashboard between amber and mint-white; a mid-fade double tap reverses without a jump.
Pressing J lowers the driver's window and its heavy-fog overlay together.
Each uniform swept min/default/max on light_fog changes the windshield fog as its range describes.
The three bound textures are the actual generated files with explicit import settings; the normal map reads as OpenGL (curl check).
Editing the light_fog material changes only the windshield; editing the shared shader line changes both windows.
Forward+ shows 137/188/225 on the data quad as predicted; Compatibility shows the file values on both quads.
Godot's generated shader renders the textures as an opaque lit surface; the hand-written fog shader is transparent with a clear centre.
Recorded suite results pass; each deliberate mutation made its test exit 1.
